title: Sep 24 Results + Sep 25 Preview: Seven Wins and the Model Found Its Command

## Sep 24 Results: Solid Command on the Mound

From a pitcher's perspective, going 7-5 is like working six strong innings—not perfect, but you gave your team a real chance to win. The model hit 58.3% yesterday, and more importantly, it found the strike zone when the confidence was high. That's what separates a quality start from a shaky outing.

## Breaking Down Yesterday's Performance

The Diamondbacks pick at 61% was textbook—high conviction, clean execution. Same with the Cubs at 60%. Those are the pitches you throw with full confidence. The Yankees call at 58% came through, and even our coin-flip Rangers pick at 50% landed right.

The Braves miss at 61% stings the most. That's like leaving a fastball over the plate with two strikes—you made the right pitch, but sometimes the hitter just gets you. The Phillies and White Sox misses were lower conviction calls, so those are easier to live with.

## Sep 25 Preview: Tomorrow's Top Pick

Looking ahead to Thursday's slate, the model is pointing us toward Fenway Park. Cubs traveling to Boston, and we're backing the Red Sox at 57% confidence.

### The Pitching Matchup Analysis

Clay Holmes gets the ball for Chicago—I know Clay from his bullpen days, and starting is a different animal. Working multiple times through a lineup requires a deeper arsenal and better command management. Alec Gamboa takes the hill for Boston, and at home in Fenway, that's where you want to trust your arm.

From a pitcher's perspective, this isn't just about stuff—it's about comfort level, routine, and knowing how to pitch in your home park. The 57% edge tells me the model sees something in the matchup dynamics and team performance that tilts toward the home side.
